name: Shadow Theatre
summary: Backlit paper shadow-puppet theatre: indigo-black cut-paper silhouettes over glowing teal, violet, crimson and amber light fields.
description: The whole floor is light: large noise-shaped colour fields (moonlit teal, dusk violet, crimson, amber) glow like a lit screen behind a puppet stage, separated by thin ink seams threaded with lace beads and covered in flat ink cut-outs (grass, leaves, filigree, stars). Everything standing on it is a single flat silhouette in near-black ink (#0b0510) built from tapered strokes, lens leaves and spiral curls in the Lotte Reiniger / Limbo tradition; the only colour on a silhouette is emissive, like carved pumpkin faces, green eyes or magenta cracks, plus a soft baked rim of light. Ghosts invert the rule and are pale glowing veils, and a theatre frame of velvet curtains and a scalloped valance closes the picture.
bestFor: survivor-likes and hordes with many enemies
rhythm games with a stage theme
avoidFor: games that need colour-coded characters (team colours, element colours on bodies)
UI-heavy strategy games with small units

difficulty.why: Silhouettes are easy to draw, but making many enemy types readable purely by their outline takes real thought.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites baked once at K = round(screenHeightPx / 360 × 1.3 × 4) / 4 px per world unit (clamped 2.5–5), ground chunks of 256 world units at up to 2.5 px/unit.
technique.summary: Every figure is filled in one ink colour from tapered limbs, leaves and spiral curls on a K-px/unit canvas; emissive parts are drawn with a radial gradient plus a shadowBlur bloom; a separate rim-light copy (8 offset tinted stamps, blurred) is added with 'lighter' behind each sprite. The ground is a per-pixel field shader with four colour bands, seam lines, light bleed, ripples and grain, plus an ink lace layer composited at 80 %.
technique.linework: No outlines at all: silhouettes are solid #0b0510 fills. Thin parts are tapered filled strokes (limb()) from w0 to w1 (e.g. 1.15 → 0.9 units for legs, 1.0 → 0.45 for leaf stems, 0.5 → 0.1 for curls) with round caps. The only 'lines' are the ground seams: 0.72 units wide (|sd| < 0.36), ink #16081c at 85 % opacity, and lace strokes 0.25–0.45 units.
technique.shading: None on silhouettes (completely flat ink). The ground has soft gradients inside each field: edge colour at the seam to core colour 0.75 field-units deep, gloss-modulated by low-frequency fbm (×0.9–1.1); amber fields get a hot #fff0c4 heart.
technique.lighting: Backlight: the floor is the light source. Characters are lit only by a warm rim (#ffb24a for the hero, #fff6dc for enemies on hit), additive radial glows around emissive faces/lanterns, and a warm follow-spot pool under the hero. Light bleeds 6 units out of every seam towards rgb(255,240,215). A purple-black vignette and curtain frame darken the edges.
technique.texture: Paper grain: 256×256 tiling Int8 noise (3×3 box blur ×3.2 + raw ×5) with 70 random-walk paper fibres (+4), added to the ground RGB (R ×1, G ×0.9, B ×0.8). Silhouettes have no texture.

palette.name: Shadow Ink
palette.role: Every silhouette, prop, curtain and HUD panel (~25–35 % of the screen)

palette.name: Lace Ink
palette.role: Ground seams and lace decals (composited at 80–85 %)

palette.name: Amber Core
palette.role: Centre of the warm amber light fields (largest field type)

palette.name: Hot Gold
palette.role: Hot heart deep inside amber fields

palette.name: Moon Teal
palette.role: Centre of moonlit teal water fields (with ripple highlights #d7fff5)

palette.name: Face Core
palette.role: Hottest centre of carved faces and lanterns

palette.name: Ember Orange
palette.role: Outer rim of carved faces; bloom rgba(255,150,40,.95)

palette.name: Crack Magenta
palette.role: Brute cracks, core and eyes (crack stroke #ffb8f0)

palette.name: HUD Gold
palette.role: HUD headings, level text, hairlines rgba(255,196,120,.55)

paletteRules: Two worlds only: glowing light (the floor and emissive parts) and flat ink (everything standing). Nothing is mid-grey or shaded.
Silhouettes are always #0b0510 at 100 % opacity; never tint a body in a field colour.
Colour on a character must be emissive and small: faces, eyes, cracks, cores. Hero = orange/gold, small enemies = acid green, brute = magenta, gems = aqua/gold.
Field ratio on screen roughly amber 40 %, crimson 30 %, violet 20 %, teal 10 %; fields always border in the order teal | violet | crimson | amber (they are thresholds of one noise value).
Ghosts are the only pale bodies; keep them cold (blue-white) so they never compete with the warm hero face.
No pure black (#000) and no saturated blues or greens in the floor besides moon teal.

typography.role: Numbers, timer, titles, level badge, damage numbers, card names
typography.css: font: 900 34px/1.05 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #ffe4a6; text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(255,170,70,1), 0 0 16px rgba(255,110,40,.8);

typography.role: Small-caps labels and hints ("until midnight", "choose with 1 · 2 · 3")
typography.css: font: 400 13px/1.2 'IM Fell English SC', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #f4c99a;

typography.role: Body text: card descriptions, stats, HUD default

background.summary: A per-pixel light shader: one domain-warped noise value f = (warped(x/1300, y/1300) − 0.5) × 9.5 + small fbm detail is cut at thresholds −0.95 / −0.3 / 0.35 into four glowing fields (teal, violet, crimson, amber). Each seam is an ink line with light bleeding out of it; teal fields get moonlit ripple lines; paper grain covers everything; a lace layer of ink decals (beads along seams, grass, leaves, filigree, dandelion clocks, stars, reeds, ripples, ferns, roots) sits on top.
layers: Field colours: 4 bands blended over ±0.075 f-units, each from edge to core colour across 0.75 f-units, × gloss 0.9–1.1
Light bleed: within 6 units of a seam lerp towards rgb(255,240,215) by (1 − d/6)² × 0.22
Teal ripples: sin(y × 0.72 + 7·perlin(x/95) + 2.5·perlin(x/33)) > 0.86 lightens towards rgb(215,255,245)
Seam line: ink #16081c at 85 % where |signed distance| < 0.36 units (anti-aliased)
Lace layer (ink, composited at 80 %): seam beads every ~4.2 units, then field-specific decals
Additive glints: 4-point light stars on violet, pale moon glints on teal ripples
Props (y-sorted, standing silhouettes): trees, gates, fences, graves, scarecrows, crow posts, lantern poles, lit pumpkins, weeds

characters.summary: Shadow puppets built from a tiny vocabulary: ellipses, tapered limbs (Catmull-Rom smoothed polylines filled as ribbons), lens leaves, spiral curls and cut-out holes, all in one ink colour, facing +x and mirrored for -x. The hero is ~18 × 33 units with a pumpkin head (four overlapping ellipses, rx 6.8, ry 5.4) whose carved face is the brightest thing on screen, a jagged cloak, streaming scarf tails and jointed puppet legs. 6 walk frames, 4 idle frames, all baked.
rules: Readability is 100 % silhouette: every actor type needs a unique outline at 30 px tall (bulb + leaf crown, veil + tail, giant gorilla bulb + antler crown, pumpkin head + cloak).
Every tip ends in a curl or a leaf – stems, toes, tails, scarf ends, crowns. Straight cut ends look wrong.
Faces are holes or emissive shapes, never painted features: carved triangles, glowing slits, a destination-out mouth cut.
Emissive colour identifies the threat class: orange/gold = hero and friendly lights, green = small enemies, magenta = brutes, cold white = ghosts.
Hero is always lit: warm #ffb24a rim at 75 % + follow-spot pool, so it pops out of any enemy crowd.
Enemies have no rim until hit; hit flash = white-cream rim added with 'lighter' at up to 90 %.
Ghosts invert: pale veil with a dark #160828 halo (blur 2.2 units, 42 %) under a light #d6f0ff halo (blur 1.4 units, 95 %).

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A baked lens-shaped seed with a #ffcf7a → #fff6d8 → #fff gradient and 1.2-unit bloom, an additive 11-unit tapered trail (rgba(255,120,30,0) → rgba(255,235,170,.9)) and an additive ember glow at 70 %.

effects.name: Hit flare
effects.how: 4-point light star (arms 9 and 6 units, lens leaves with gradients) + radial core, added with 'lighter' for 0.16 s, plus 3 short additive spark streaks.

effects.name: Paper crumble death
effects.how: The silhouette is pre-cut into 5 (brute 7) torn wedge shards along jagged radial lines; each shard's cut edge is stroked #ff9a3a (0.9 units, source-atop). Shards fly out, rotate and fall with alpha 1 − u² over ~0.6 s, plus paper scraps and embers.

effects.name: Embers
effects.how: Tiny additive radial sprites (3-unit radius: white → rgba(255,190,80,.85) → transparent) rising with negative gravity and flickering 0.7–1.0 at 30 Hz; cold (blue-white) and pink variants.

effects.name: Spawn
effects.how: Enemies rise out of a slot in the stage like a puppet on a stick: outBack ease from 95 % of their height below the floor, clipped at the floor line, a 0.7-unit ink rod underneath and an additive warm slot glow.

effects.name: Level-up ring
effects.how: An additive ring of radius 10.5 units with 12 small 4-point stars on it and a 1.2-unit bloom, expanding with outQuad, plus a large flare and 14 embers.

effects.name: Dash
effects.how: Three trailing copies of the current frame tinted rgba(20,6,26,1), alpha 0.4/i, spaced 6 units back, plus ember trail.

effects.name: Gems
effects.how: Ink teardrop with an inner glass gradient (#fff → #b8fff4 → #3fe0d8), an additive cyan glow pulsing 0.75–1.0, bobbing ±0.8 units; big gems are gold with a slowly rotating flare.

ui.summary: HUD pieces are ink (#0b0510) plates with a hairline gold ring (rgba(255,196,120,.55)) between two ink rings and a warm outer glow; bars have glowing gradient fills; text is Cinzel with ink + orange glow shadows. Level-up cards are lit stage scenes: amber-to-crimson radial gradient behind an ink curtain-and-valance cut-out with an ink stage lip.

motion: Hero: 6-frame walk cycle advanced at anim × 1.5 (≈ 9 fps at normal speed), 4-frame idle at 2.6 fps; head bob −|cos| × 0.9 units, scarf tails wave at 2× the step phase.
Small enemy: 6 frames at 4.8 per anim second, plus a whole-sprite rocking wobble of ±0.075 rad (puppet on a rod).
Brute: 6 frames at 3.6 per anim second, wobble ±0.035 rad, magenta core glow pulsing 0.45 ± 0.25 at 4 rad/s.
Ghost: 4 frames at 6 fps, hovering 2.2 units up with ±1.2-unit bob (3.1 rad/s) and ±0.06 rad sway.
Props sway like hinged puppets: trees ±0.012 rad, scarecrows ±0.02 rad at 0.7 rad/s; weeds ±0.05 rad at 1.3 rad/s.
Candle flicker on faces and lanterns: 0.8 + 0.12·sin(11t) + 0.08·sin(27t).
Damage numbers pop from 1.6× to 1× in 0.08 s and fade over the last 0.25 s.
do: Make the floor the brightest, most colourful thing; keep all standing objects flat ink.
Build every shape from tapered limbs, lens leaves and spiral curls, and finish tips with a curl.
Give each enemy class a unique silhouette and one emissive colour (green, magenta, cold white).
Keep the hero permanently rim-lit and standing in a warm follow-spot pool.
Bake everything (frames, rims, mirrored copies, glows, shards) once at load and only blit per frame.
Add light with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' (glows, rims, embers, flares), never by brightening ink.
Frame the screen as a stage: curtains, scalloped valance with tassels, vignette, stage lip.
dont: Don't outline silhouettes or shade them with gradients – a lit edge comes only from the additive rim sprite.
Don't paint eyes or mouths in body colour; carve them (destination-out) or make them emissive.
Don't use more than one emissive colour per character type, or warm emissives on enemies that would rival the hero face.
Don't let decals become as dense as the actors – lace sits at 80 % and is much finer (0.25–0.85 unit strokes).
Don't use pure black, grey or photographic textures; ink is indigo-black #0b0510.
Don't apply ctx.filter or shadowBlur per frame – bake it.
Don't make the light fields small and busy; they should be hundreds of units across.
performance: All sprites are baked once in init: hero 6 walk + 4 idle frames, each with rim and hurt-rim copies and mirrored versions; small enemy 2 variants × 6 frames; ghost 4; brute 6; plus torn-shard sets, glows and 20 prop sprites. Rim light costs 8 drawImage + 1 blur filter per frame at bake time. Per frame only drawImage blits with transforms and a few 'lighter' composites run. The ground is the expensive part: per 256-unit chunk a 4-unit noise grid (warped fbm, ~70×70) and a per-pixel loop (bilinear + bleed + ripples + grain + seam) at up to 2.5 px/unit, computed as a generator that yields every 2 rows so chunks stream in without hitches; the lace layer is drawn with vector paths into an offscreen canvas then composited once. The theatre frame overlay is baked per screen size.
